value.a: THE PRIOR-ART GATE CHANGED THE CAST'S SHAPE, WHICH IS THE GATE EARNING ITS KEEP. The intent was going to BUILD a record of the apprentice's calls; the consult found it already on disk and complete on the ask side, so the build shrank to a reader plus a parse fix. And the thing that would have been re-derived was a WORSE version: anything CC built at the shim would have missed aider's own system prompt and repo map by construction, because the shim never sees them.

A WRITE-ONLY RECORD READS AS NO RECORD, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS TWO. Append-only and complete on the ask side since the device was built; two readers in all of cairn/, both aggregating or printing, neither returning a row. The rows were never missing — the door out of them was. The tell that this is Law 10's ordinary state rather than an absence: it dissolved the moment somebody asked to READ instead of to build.

AN INSTRUMENT CANNOT AUDIT WHAT IT SITS UPSTREAM OF. Brief.unsourced() runs before aider wraps our prompt, so aider_shim's clause (7) has always been asserted over our half of a composite nobody saw whole. Generalises past this seam: any 'nothing enters here but X' claim wants its instrument DOWNSTREAM of the last thing that can add.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT MADE THE CAST HONEST. The bytes UP are recorded; the bytes DOWN are parsed and dropped. Recording the response body while waving the request half through would leave the record asymmetric in exactly the direction that hides OUR additions rather than the host's — which is why the assembly hop between `canonical` and the posted payload rides the falsifier instead of the confidence.

THE PIECE THIS CAST STOPPED. A SCAFFOLD span asking the apprentice to report what is wrong was one edit from being built, landing in a 4000-char tail. Akien's redirect — 'the inference domain is supposed to create a inference ticket' — did not reject the piece, it named the record the piece's answer needed. The piece survives, reordered: the ticket first, the question second.

NOT IN SCOPE AND SAID SO: semantic canonicalization (T1.3) and active falsifier invalidation (T1.4), both filed edges on inference_domain's charter, neither touched. This ticket makes the existing rows readable and complete; it does not make them smarter.
